entities.summary: Setau was the Viceroy of Kush in the second half of Ramesses II's reign. Contemporary records show that Setau served in this position from Year 38 until at least Year 63 of Ramesses II's reign. Setau was "a graduate of the royal school" and already enjoyed an impressive record of royal service which is detailed in a long autobiographical inscription carved at Wadi es-Sebua. The temple of Wadi es-Sebua was built for Ramesses II by Setau around 1236 BC or Year 44 of this pharaoh's reign. Eleven of his stela, now in the Cairo Museum, were found in the courtyard of this temple and make it possible to establish his career and understand the precise duties of a viceroy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a viceroy of Kush under Ramesses II, Setau played a crucial role in maintaining regional stability and overseeing the construction of significant temples. His autobiographical inscription provides valuable insights into the administrative and architectural achievements of ancient Egypt during this period.
